searchText: Does it even make sense post-merge? Given the current proposal on how to deal with difficulty I think the question would be if anyone is on board to implementing it post-merge and how. There is at least one person who thinks it's useful post-merge <https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/2481> ^exactly, the earlier discussion also ties into it. Is calcification post-Merge an acceptable or desirable outcome? (q1) Micah was in favour of bomb to avoid coordination failure in implementing new features we've already agreed we want implemented. But coordination between whom? 4 client teams? (q2) As ethereum governance currently stands, client teams have very asymmetric power, they can ask everyone else to shove it and do what they want (Peter from geth pretty much said this on twitter). As long as this stands we don't need a bomb for coordination among the broader community of ETH holders or users, because it isn't their coordination that's actually needed. And all teams trivially know how to diffuse the bomb ofcourse. Bomb is not going to force a feature update if one of the client teams is fundamentally opposed to something. And all teams are on discord, they don't need a bomb if they wanna open or retain communication lines. Would be keen to know his arguments. Also would a separate channel or discord be good for governance issues? ETH magicians is not async I think we’re kind of hitting diminishing returns discussing the bomb as it relates to the current issue, which is the London activation. I recommend starting an Ethereum Magicians thread for further discussion at this point. Half of ETH magicians threads are dead, also they aren't as conducive to 1-to-1 conversation. Would a place for shorter form async discussion be good? (like discord) The challenge is people have a limited attention span, and what makes this discord work well is we try and keep it relatively focused on technical issues. I’m very cautious of losing the high signal from this discord if we broaden the discussion to more abstract governance-related topics. Perhaps one way forward with EthMag is to organize a call or more synchronous discussion there? Definitely not saying to have it in same channels as this discord, am suggesting either new section of channels or else new server altogether. Organising call is an even larger barrier, and hard to do for not official contributors. Plenty of things continue to be discussed on ethmagicians. It’s also a much better historical record of things than a few hundred discord messages and is often easier to engage with because it doesn’t require immediate synchronous presence Did you guys decide to postpone London and work on extending the unit test coverage and/or fuzzing suite? Or you just crossed fingers? 😅 Just checked, London introduces a TON of breaking changes no plan to postpone london at this time You know, the closer we are to the fork block, the harder it will be to accomplish that And there is quite a lot to risk. At the end of the day, ETH is the second cryptocurrency with a quarter trillion market cap we discussed it on acd 118, the decision was made to not postpone the fork I've been sending a lot of fuzzing transactions on goerli, some that hit the assertion that broke (they were rejected as expected) and lots that execute the BASEFEE opcode. > just crossed fingers I think this devalues all the hard work the client and testing teams have put in over the last couple of months. "Just crossed fingers" is still an ample summary. 1559 has so much more corner cases than a small assertion that blew up Ropsten. TBH given that Berlin had a consensus bug, I'm afraid 1559 will cause one on mainnet as well. Also it'll be interesting to see the exact dynamics of 1559 play out on mainnet, because so far we only have theoretical game theory predictions. I have a gut feeling that we'll have something along the lines of CREATE2 + SELFDESTRUCT That is some dynamics we could never predict But this is not a consensus bug per se, so I rest my case > still an ample summary Truthfully though, it's neither ample nor a summary. It's a nonconstructive belittlement. We can raise the level of discourse above that. If you don't like the tone, don't read it. The sentiment is still there and it is based on reasonable doubt. Anyhow. One thought I've had is that it would be interesting to see is if someone could model the system with TLA+ and run it through its paces that way. In the area of consensus algorithms, new algorithms are basically never accepted or even reviewed without a TLA+ spec. For example, like the Raft TLA+ spec. https://github.com/ongardie/raft.tla I've seen some attempts at this with Ethereum, but nothing ever complete. It would be rather interesting to see, yes I'm seeing a _lot_ of reorgs on goerli for the last ~90m or so. For example around block 5203861 seems like it reorg'ed 4 different times, with multiple reorgs of each block before and after too. https://gist.github.com/ryanschneider/9d2cab3b08815e8e96b045398c42f86f 13 reorgs in a 205 second period, this node has seen 280 reorgs from 16:00 to 17:47 UTC. Mentioning here in case it's indicative of any issues w/ the recent London releases. Might be, I'm sending a lot of transactions... Could be that some signers didn't update to the latest release yet ``` INFO [07-25|15:47:18.270] 😱 block lost number=5,203,801 hash=eafb40..433da6 ``` I don't recall seeing that message before on our signer Thats when your signed block gets dropped from the canonical chain ya looks to be somewhat common, I just never noticed it The nethermind sealer seems to be offline for a day, I'm currently syncing a nethermind node to see if that is just incidental or an issue <@&652918665943056397> We checked our node and it looks like it is working fine. We're sealing blocks https://goerli.etherscan.io/address/0x4c2ae482593505f0163cdefc073e81c63cda4107#mine I assume that you checked in ethstats https://stats.goerli.net/ so maybe it is something wrong with reporting or with configuration of ethstats. We need to check it 🙂
